adaptive.label: Adaptive practice
adaptive.definition: The next difficulty is picked from your results. Patient behaviour is adjusted to exercise your weakest rubric domain.

rubric.label: Rubric
rubric.definition: The scoring guide used to assess your conversation and write-up. Feedback explains each domain with evidence from your visit.

rating.label: Skill rating
rating.definition: A number that changes when you perform above or below the expected outcome at a difficulty level. It is not a percentage of mastery.

variation.label: Patient variation
variation.definition: A retry can change the patient's mood and way of speaking. The clinical facts stay the same.

draft.label: AI draft
draft.definition: A fictional case written by AI that faculty have not reviewed. Use it for practice; its content is not clinically validated.

vitals.label: Vital signs
vitals.definition: Basic measures of body function: temperature, pulse, breathing rate and blood pressure.

cbc.label: Complete blood count (CBC)
cbc.definition: A blood test that measures blood cells, including red cells, white cells and platelets.

lipids.label: Lipid panel
lipids.definition: A blood test measuring cholesterol and triglycerides, which are fats in the blood.

sbar.label: SBAR
sbar.definition: A structured handoff: Situation, Background, Assessment, and Recommendation or Request.

polyuria.label: Polyuria
polyuria.definition: Passing an unusually large volume of urine, rather than simply going more often.

enuresis.label: Enuresis
enuresis.definition: Involuntary wetting. Nocturnal enuresis means wetting during sleep.

acanthosis.label: Acanthosis nigricans
acanthosis.definition: Areas of darker, thickened skin with a velvety texture, often in skin folds.

a1c.label: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c)
a1c.definition: A blood test summarizing blood sugar levels over roughly the previous two to three months.

dka.label: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)
dka.definition: A dangerous complication of diabetes in which ketones build up and make the blood too acidic.

cpeptide.label: C-peptide
cpeptide.definition: A substance released when the body makes insulin. Measuring it helps estimate the body’s own insulin production.

urinalysis.label: Urinalysis
urinalysis.definition: Testing a urine sample for clues about health and disease.

differential.label: Differential diagnosis
differential.definition: A set of possible explanations for symptoms that is narrowed using history, examination and tests.

hyperglycemia.label: Hyperglycemia
hyperglycemia.definition: Blood sugar that is higher than normal.

glucose.label: Blood glucose
glucose.definition: The sugar in the blood that provides energy to the body’s cells.

opening_and_purpose.label: Opening and purpose
opening_and_purpose.definition: Introduce yourself and your role, agree on the patient’s main concern, and explain what the visit will cover.

rapport_respect_empathy.label: Rapport, respect, and empathy
rapport_respect_empathy.definition: Build trust by listening attentively, respecting the patient’s perspective, and acknowledging feelings without judgment.

information_gathering.label: Information gathering
information_gathering.definition: Use open questions and focused follow-ups to learn the relevant history, symptoms, risks, and patient goals.

listening_and_response_to_cues.label: Listening and response to cues
listening_and_response_to_cues.definition: Notice concerns, uncertainty, and inconsistencies in the patient’s story, then clarify them without interrupting.

explanation_and_shared_decisions.label: Explanation and shared decisions
explanation_and_shared_decisions.definition: Explain findings and options in plain language, check understanding, and agree on next steps with the patient.

clinical_reasoning_and_synthesis.label: Clinical reasoning and synthesis
clinical_reasoning_and_synthesis.definition: Connect the history, examination, and test results to form an assessment. Consider alternatives, uncertainty, and warning signs.

professionalism_safety_closure.label: Professionalism, safety, and closure
professionalism_safety_closure.definition: Respect privacy and boundaries, explain limitations, and close with a clear plan for follow-up and when to seek help.

intro.label: Professional introduction
intro.definition: Introduce your role and use respectful, empathetic language throughout the visit.

needs_dx.label: Age at hearing-loss diagnosis
needs_dx.definition: Find out when hearing loss was identified and how it has affected the patient.

needs_device.label: Hearing-device use
needs_device.definition: Ask about hearing aids or implants, how they are used, and any difficulties.

needs_aud.label: Other auditory complaints
needs_aud.definition: Ask about additional hearing symptoms, including ringing in the ears or sound sensitivity.

needs_edu.label: Educational needs
needs_edu.definition: Explore learning needs and the support needed in school or other educational settings.

needs_comm.label: Communication needs
needs_comm.definition: Ask which everyday listening or communication challenge matters most to the patient today.

audio_sev.label: Hearing-loss severity
audio_sev.definition: Explain the hearing-test results clearly and sensitively, including their impact on communication.

audio_banana.label: Speech Banana
audio_banana.definition: An audiogram region showing where common speech sounds fall in pitch and loudness.

exp_roles.label: Audiologist and SLP roles
exp_roles.definition: Explain how an audiologist supports hearing and a speech-language pathologist supports communication.

exp_rehab.label: Aural rehabilitation
exp_rehab.definition: Support and training that help someone make use of hearing and communicate more effectively.

exp_empathy.label: Expressing empathy
exp_empathy.definition: Acknowledge the patient’s feelings and the effect of their difficulties on daily life.

exp_questions.label: Answering patient questions
exp_questions.definition: Invite questions and give understandable answers that address the patient’s concerns.

melena.label: Melena
melena.definition: Black, tar-like stool caused by digested blood, usually from bleeding higher in the digestive tract.

anemia.label: Anemia
anemia.definition: Too few healthy red blood cells or too little hemoglobin to carry enough oxygen.

hemoglobin.label: Hemoglobin
hemoglobin.definition: The protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.

microcytosis.label: Microcytosis
microcytosis.definition: Red blood cells that are smaller than usual; their size is measured by MCV.

mcv.label: Mean corpuscular volume (MCV)
mcv.definition: A measure of the average size of red blood cells.

ferritin.label: Ferritin
ferritin.definition: A protein that stores iron. A ferritin blood test helps assess iron stores.

tibc.label: Total iron-binding capacity (TIBC)
tibc.definition: A blood test assessing how much iron blood proteins can bind.

iron_studies.label: Iron studies
iron_studies.definition: A group of blood tests checking iron levels, iron transport, and stored iron.

transferrin.label: Transferrin
transferrin.definition: A protein that transports iron in the blood.

nsaids.label: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)
nsaids.definition: Medicines such as ibuprofen and naproxen that reduce pain and inflammation. They can increase stomach bleeding risk.

naproxen.label: Naproxen
naproxen.definition: An NSAID used for pain and inflammation.

colonoscopy.label: Colonoscopy
colonoscopy.definition: An examination of the inside of the large intestine using a flexible camera.

dyspnea.label: Dyspnea
dyspnea.definition: The feeling of difficult or uncomfortable breathing, often called shortness of breath.

edema.label: Edema
edema.definition: Swelling caused by fluid collecting in body tissues.

pallor.label: Pallor
pallor.definition: An unusually pale appearance of the skin or mucous membranes.

cyanosis.label: Cyanosis
cyanosis.definition: A bluish appearance of the skin or mucous membranes, which can indicate low oxygen.

creatinine.label: Creatinine
creatinine.definition: A waste product from muscles. Blood levels help assess how well the kidneys filter waste.

hpi.label: History of present illness (HPI)
hpi.definition: The story of the current problem: onset, course, symptoms, relevant context, and what makes it better or worse.

otc.label: Over-the-counter (OTC)
otc.definition: A medicine available without a prescription. Include these medicines when reviewing medication use.

ros.label: Review of systems (ROS)
ros.definition: Questions about symptoms across body systems to identify additional relevant problems.

soap.label: SOAP note
soap.definition: A structured write-up: Subjective, Objective, Assessment, and Plan.

safety_net.label: Safety-net plan
safety_net.definition: Clear instructions about what to watch for, when to seek help, and how follow-up will happen.

red_flags.label: Red flags
red_flags.definition: Warning findings that may need urgent assessment or a change in the care plan.

medication_reconciliation.label: Medication reconciliation
medication_reconciliation.definition: Compare the patient’s actual medicine use with the record and resolve differences, including doses and nonprescription medicines.

open_question.label: Open-ended question
open_question.definition: A question that lets the patient describe their experience in their own words instead of giving a yes/no answer.

history_taking.label: History-taking
history_taking.definition: Gather the patient’s story, medical background, medication use, and relevant personal context.

differential_short.label: Working differential
differential_short.definition: The current list of plausible explanations, updated as more evidence is gathered.

prior_records.label: Prior records
prior_records.definition: Earlier notes, test results, and reports that provide context for the current visit.

self_intro.label: Self-introduction
self_intro.definition: Tell the patient your name and role, and explain why you are meeting today.

teach_back.label: Teach-back
teach_back.definition: Ask the patient to explain the plan in their own words so you can check how clearly you explained it.
